title: Public Pressure and Corporate Tax Behavior

scopes.description: Complete author workflow for reproducing the online appendix analyses in Tables A1–A8 and the accompanying robustness/bootstrap discussions. The package contains only the appendix PDF, so there is no runnable entry point or established dependency closure.

requirements.description: Author-compatible input data sufficient to reproduce the empirical results in appendix Tables A1–A8 and the associated analyses are required. The appendix reports firm-level estimation samples, subsidiary disclosure measures, and bootstrap/randomization results, but supplies no data or data specification; the prepared input product(s), identifiers, full fields/history, transformations, and compatible acquisition route are undetermined. Source mentions such as Compustat, ActionAid, and media-search terms are clarification leads; without the author workflow they do not establish separate mandatory live raw-source requirements.

issues.description: The assessed package contains only an online appendix PDF. It provides result tables and methodological notes but no executable author code, data description, datasets, README, or entry-point instructions, so the complete software requirements and table-by-table producer/consumer workflow cannot be established.

evidence.description: The appendix enumerates supplemental output Tables A1–A8 and associated sensitivity analyses.
evidence.quote: Summary of the Tables Table A1: The Role of Hidden (Undisclosed) Tax Haven Subsidiaries in the Pre-pressure Period

evidence.description: Table A1 reports an empirical FTSE 100 analysis, sample size, and bootstrap inference.
Table A8 describes a subsidiary analysis using cases for which ActionAid publicly disclosed data; the package provides no corresponding dataset or location.
evidence.quote: subsidiary disclosure for the FTSE 100 firms for which ActionAid publicly disclosed the data—one observation per firm.

evidence.description: The appendix describes random assignment and repeated estimation for bootstrap/randomization analyses, but includes no runnable implementation.
evidence.quote: We assemble a random distribution of coefficients for Model 1 by randomly assigning the designation of compliant versus non-complaint and estimating Model 1 1,000 times.

evidence.description: The frozen static audit inventories only the appendix PDF and reports no supported code, entry points, or dependency edges.

actions.description: Request the author replication workflow and input specifications for the complete appendix analysis set.
steps: Request the executable author code or an approved replacement workflow, including supporting programs, software/version details, run instructions, execution order, and a mapping of every listed Table A1–A8 analysis and bootstrap/randomization result to its producer.

Request the author-prepared analysis data or a verified acquisition route, with file/product format, identifiers, required fields, covered years, sample definitions, transformations, and access conditions. Ask how the Appendix’s ActionAid and other source references relate to the prepared input; do not infer independent raw-source requirements from these references alone.
After receipt, trace each actual producer-consumer handoff, including any separate companion analysis, and revise the dependency closure only from supplied workflow evidence.
validation: Confirm that every Table A1–A8 result and the bootstrap/randomization analyses have a supplied entry point and documented producer chain.
Check the received input specification against author-defined samples, variables, periods, and transformations before treating any route as compatible.
Only after a separate authorized execution, compare reproduced sample counts and table outputs with the appendix; preserve all author-described samples and resampling procedures.

review_notes: This is an appendix-only release. The cited Compustat, ActionAid, and media-search references are useful leads for author clarification, but no executable workflow or data route establishes them as separate live raw inputs.
No analysis_only scope is supported because there is no supplied analysis code or author-prepared analysis dataset.
